**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/29 (Mon) 02:25
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The point of discussing bones, discs, and ligaments is to illustrate the complexity of the spine and how easily it can go wrong and cause pain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The essence of Jeremy’s technique is that it focuses on the whole rather than the details of what has gone wrong.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user’s complicated back is an integrated whole, which includes muscles that have not yet been discussed.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] If the whole is working correctly, the details will often resolve themselves, but not always.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is important to remember the intricacy of the spine when performing exercises as instructed by Jeremy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Doing exercises incorrectly can be worse than not doing them at all.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The core muscles, which support the spine, are located between the shoulders and hips, encompassing the front, back, and sides of the body.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tending to the core is a serious responsibility and requires significant exercise.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The small muscles called “paraspinals” stabilize the spine and relay information to the brain about the spine's position.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overloaded paraspinal muscles can lead to painful spasms and debilitating pain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Poor posture can cause larger muscles, like the glutes, to become inactive, leading to reliance on the paraspinals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] When larger muscles fall asleep, weight shifts to the paraspinals, which can fail and put pressure on the spine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The body has multiple layers of muscles, with the deepest ones being crucial for maintaining a neutral spine.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The “psoas” muscle is a main hip flexor that attaches to the lumbar spine and can cause issues when tight or shortened.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Prolonged sitting or sleeping in a fetal position can lead to a tight psoas muscle.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Many back muscles are “extensors,” which help with bending backward and maintaining posture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The abdominal muscles are critical for maintaining a strong and healthy back.
